scenes.heading: CI/CD for Data Pipelines
scenes.subheading: Bringing dbt and Airflow into the pipeline
scenes.narration: Data pipelines deserve the same CI/CD rigor as application code, and dbt and Airflow both fit naturally into that workflow.

scenes.heading: What to automate for data
bullets: Compile and lint dbt models on every PR
Run dbt tests against a CI warehouse
Validate Airflow DAGs import without errors
Deploy models and DAGs only after tests pass
scenes.narration: On every pull request you should compile and lint your dbt models to catch syntax and style issues. You then run dbt tests against a dedicated CI warehouse to verify data assumptions hold. You validate that every Airflow DAG imports cleanly so no broken workflow reaches the scheduler. And only after all checks pass do you deploy the models and DAGs.

scenes.heading: A dbt CI flow
scenes.narration: The flow starts when an engineer opens a pull request. Continuous integration runs dbt build against an isolated CI schema so it never touches production. dbt executes tests, ideally on just the changed models and their downstream dependencies to keep runs fast. Once everything is green, the change merges and deploys.

scenes.heading: dbt in CI
scenes.code:
name: dbt-ci
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  dbt:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      DBT_TARGET: ci
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: pip install dbt-snowflake
      - run: dbt deps
      - run: dbt build --select state:modified+ --defer --state ./prod-manifest
scenes.narration: This workflow runs on every pull request against a CI target so production data stays untouched. After installing dbt and its packages, the key command is dbt build with a state selector. The modified-plus selector runs only the models you changed and everything downstream, while deferring unchanged upstream models to production, which makes CI both fast and safe.

scenes.heading: Ship SQL blind vs test in CI
scenes.narration: Without CI, broken SQL and silent data quality bugs slip straight into production and force painful hotfixes. With CI for data, compilation errors and failing data tests are caught right in the pull request, so every merge and deploy happens with confidence.

scenes.text: Treat SQL and DAGs like software: lint, test on an isolated CI environment, and deploy only what passes.
scenes.narration: The principle is to treat your SQL models and DAGs like software by linting them, testing on an isolated CI environment, and deploying only what passes.
